items.title: Tata Elxsi inks pact with Sarla Aviation to make air taxi platform Shunya
items.summary:
Design and technology services firm Tata Elxsi on Tuesday said it has signed an initial pact with startup Sarla Aviation to collaborate on the development of the Bengaluru-based firm's air taxi platform Shunya.
Under the collaboration, Tata Elxsi will provide engineering support across avionics, including flight control systems, software integration, testing, verification and validation, and certification.
On the other hand, Sarla Aviation will lead the design, development and type certification of the Shunya platform, the company said.
The engagement also creates opportunities to extend support across sensor fusion-based navigation software, industrial and structural design, and airworthiness test support, it added.

items.title: Amazon Now plans to expand quick-commerce footprint to 300 cities soon
items.summary:
Amazon's quick commerce business unit, Amazon Now, plans to expand its footprint to 300 cities nationwide soon, a top company official said on Tuesday.
"We are expanding very rapidly. We have a path to expand to about 300 cities very, very soon," Nishant Sardana, Director - Amazon Now, told PTI here.
Amazon Now, launched in January, 2025, is currently operates in about 30 cities.
Without specifying a timeframe for realising the plan to enter 300 cities, Sardana said the company is "quadrupling" its efforts to make it happen as fast as it can.
Since its launch, Amazon Now has been doing very well, growing about 20-25 per cent month-on-month, he said.
The quick commerce industry in the country is estimated to be about USD 20 billion a year, he said, without commenting on Amazon Now's share in it.
Amazon Now has invested Rs 2,800 crores, largely on setting up infrastructure and "partner safety and well-being," he said.

items.title: Live: Choppy day for markets, oil above $92; Rupee recovers to 94.8/$ | Closing Bell
items.summary: Indian equity markets remained under pressure, with the Sensex falling 200 points and the Nifty slipping below the 24,000 mark. Market breadth weakened further as declines outpaced advances, while most sectoral indices traded lower. FMCG and IT stocks emerged as relative outperformers in an otherwise choppy session. Auto stocks declined following the release of August monthly sales data, adding to the broader market pressure. The Nifty Midcap index snapped its two-day winning streak, while the Nifty Smallcap index extended its losses for another session. In commodities, Brent crude climbed back above $92 per barrel, keeping investors cautious amid ongoing global uncertainties. The rupee, however, recovered 28 paise to trade at 94.8 against the US dollar. Among Nifty 50 stocks, ITC, HCL Technologies and Adani Ports were the top gainers, while Shriram Finance, Maruti Suzuki and InterGlobe Aviation featured among the biggest losers.
